issues.message: current source at (0.006, 0.006, 0.004) (component ex) sits at z = 4mm, an E node whose adjacent cells differ by 200% (500µm below, 1.5mm above). z is one of this component's two TRANSVERSE axes, so its control volume takes the DUAL spacing 1mm there — not the primal cell 1.5mm — and the realized current moment would be off by 1.500x on this axis alone if the primal cell were used (issue #672). That IS handled, but a source on a grading step is where the injected amplitude is most mesh-sensitive: move it onto a locally uniform node if its amplitude is claims-bearing.

dz_profile max adjacent cell ratio 3.000 exceeds the validated multi-band grading cap 1.4 (docs/guides/support_matrix.md, 'Multi-band graded mesh'). WHY: stability is unaffected (dt is the global min-cell CFL, sufficient on any tensor grid), but per-transition accuracy is witnessed only along z and only up to ratio 1.4 — the -54 dB reflection class at 30 cells/wavelength (it scales as (dz/lambda)^2), against -44 dB measured at ratio 2.0. COST: an unquantified reflection and grading-dispersion error at that transition. REMEDY: split it into ratio<=1.4 steps (e.g. rfx.smooth_grading) to stay inside the validated envelope, or accept it and say so in the report. STALE-IF: the support-matrix row raises the cap.
